name: hash-sha384-short
algorithm: std SHA-384 over every 64-byte message of splitmix64 bytes, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-sha384-short.mk).

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard SHA-384; OpenSSL's portable C is a third-party library, and no third-party code stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)
skip.rust: no std SHA-384: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); the sha2 crate is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Idiomatic standard library, the short-message case (HKDF-Expand-Label and HMAC-SHA-384 hash short blocks): one one-shot call per 64-byte message, one 128-byte block each with the padding, so Sum's padding and the 48-byte truncation are half the work. Messages per second = mib * 1048576 / 64 * reps / median.

Go: crypto/sha512 computes the message schedule with AVX2 on amd64 when the CPU has it, whatever GOAMD64 says (run-time dispatch in the library); Mk's Sha384 does too since M9 item 11.24a (D-775): an AVX2 message schedule beside rounds compiled with bmi2 when the CPU has avx2 and bmi2 (run-time dispatch), else Sha512's scalar loop. Zig at x86_64_v2 is scalar. Labelled: on a CPU with avx2 and bmi2 the zig cell compares instruction sets as well as libraries; before D-775 the go cell did (status/std-hash2.md, H2-6).

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off, Go 1.27.3, owner's machine, 2026-11-12); the Mk (mk build --release) and Zig 0.17.0 (-O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2) columns printed the same in `go run ./tools/bench verify -publish-size` (status/std-hash2.md, fix round). Written by the std-hash2 lane for review finding H2-8. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
